sections.summary: Simon Sinek opens with the story of Captain William Swenson, who ran into live fire to rescue wounded soldiers in Afghanistan. A GoPro camera captured Swenson kissing a wounded soldier before returning to save more. This powerful image raises the question: where does such selfless love come from?
sections.summaryKo: 사이먼 사이넥이 아프가니스탄에서 부상병을 구하기 위해 실탄이 오가는 속으로 뛰어든 캡틴 윌리엄 스웬슨의 이야기로 시작해요. 고프로 카메라가 스웬슨이 부상병에게 입맞춤하고 다시 구조하러 돌아가는 장면을 담았어요. 이 강렬한 이미지가 질문을 던져요: 이런 이타적인 사랑은 어디서 오는 걸까?
keyPoints: Captain Swenson received the Congressional Medal of Honor
He ran into live fire to rescue the wounded
A GoPro captured his tender moment with a wounded soldier
Sinek asks: where do people like that come from?

sections.summary: Sinek contrasts the military, which rewards self-sacrifice, with business, which rewards sacrificing others. His initial assumption was that military heroes are just better people, but he learned the real answer: it's the environment. With the right conditions, everyone has the capacity for remarkable selflessness.
sections.summaryKo: 사이넥은 자기 희생을 보상하는 군대와 타인의 희생을 보상하는 비즈니스를 대비해요. 처음에는 군인 영웅들이 그냥 더 나은 사람이라고 생각했지만, 진짜 답은 환경이라는 걸 배웠어요. 올바른 환경이 갖춰지면 모든 사람에게 놀라운 이타심의 능력이 있어요.
keyPoints: Military gives medals for self-sacrifice; business gives bonuses for sacrificing others
It's not about better people — it's about the environment
The right environment unlocks everyone's capacity for remarkable things

sections.summary: Heroes he interviewed all say the same thing: 'They would have done it for me.' Trust and cooperation are feelings, not instructions. You cannot simply command people to trust or cooperate — it must come naturally from within.
sections.summaryKo: 그가 인터뷰한 영웅들은 모두 같은 말을 해요: '그들도 나를 위해 그렇게 했을 거야.' 신뢰와 협력은 감정이지 지시가 아니에요. 사람들에게 신뢰하라, 협력하라고 명령할 수 없어요 — 자연스럽게 내면에서 우러나와야 해요.
keyPoints: 'They would have done it for me' — universal answer from heroes
Trust and cooperation are feelings, not instructions
You cannot command someone to trust you

sections.section: The Circle of Safety: 50,000 Years of Evolution
sections.summary: Going back 50,000 years, humans evolved as social animals. They formed tribes — 'circles of safety' — where belonging generated trust and cooperation. Those inside could sleep at night knowing others watched for danger. Without trust, the survival system breaks down.
sections.summaryKo: 5만 년 전으로 돌아가면, 인간은 사회적 동물로 진화했어요. 부족을 형성했는데, 이것이 '안전의 원'이에요. 소속감이 신뢰와 협력을 만들어냈어요. 안에 있는 사람들은 다른 사람이 위험을 감시해준다는 걸 알기에 밤에 잠들 수 있었어요. 신뢰 없이는 생존 시스템이 무너져요.
keyPoints: Humans evolved as social animals in a dangerous world
The 'circle of safety' concept: tribes where people felt they belonged
Safety produces trust and cooperation naturally
Without trust, the survival system fails

sections.section: Modern Organizations Mirror the Paleolithic Era
sections.summary: The modern world mirrors the Paleolithic era: external threats like economic uncertainty, new technology, and competition are constants we cannot control. The only variable is conditions inside the organization. When leaders prioritize people's safety over tangible results, remarkable things happen.
sections.summaryKo: 현대 세계는 구석기 시대를 반영해요: 경제적 불확실성, 신기술, 경쟁 같은 외부 위협은 우리가 통제할 수 없는 상수예요. 유일한 변수는 조직 내부의 조건이에요. 리더가 가시적 결과보다 사람들의 안전을 우선시하면 놀라운 일이 일어나요.
keyPoints: External threats (economy, technology, competition) are uncontrollable constants
Internal conditions are the only variable — and that's where leadership matters
Leaders set the tone by putting people's safety first

sections.summary: Sinek shares the story of an airline gate agent who mistreated a passenger — not because she was a bad person, but because she didn't feel safe from her leaders. He contrasts this with Southwest Airlines, where employees don't fear leadership. Great leadership is like great parenting: providing opportunity, education, and discipline so people can achieve more than we imagined.
sections.summaryKo: 사이넥은 승객을 함부로 대한 항공사 직원의 이야기를 들려줘요 — 나쁜 사람이어서가 아니라 리더로부터 안전하다고 느끼지 못했기 때문이에요. 직원들이 리더십을 두려워하지 않는 사우스웨스트 항공과 대비해요. 훌륭한 리더십은 훌륭한 부모됨과 같아요: 기회, 교육, 훈육을 제공해서 사람들이 우리가 상상한 것 이상을 이룰 수 있게 하는 거예요.
keyPoints: Airline gate agent story: she mistreated passengers because she felt unsafe
Southwest Airlines succeeds because employees don't fear their leaders
Unsafe conditions force people to protect themselves from each other
Great leaders are like great parents — they help people grow

sections.section: Three Cases: NextJump, Banking CEOs, Bob Chapman
sections.summary: Three powerful examples: Charlie Kim's lifetime employment policy at NextJump treats employees like family. Banking CEOs with disproportionate bonuses violated the social contract of leadership by sacrificing people for numbers. Bob Chapman of Barry-Wehmiller chose furloughs over layoffs during the 2008 recession, saying 'better we all suffer a little than any suffer a lot' — morale rose, they saved $20M, and employees spontaneously traded furlough weeks to help each other.
sections.summaryKo: 세 가지 강력한 사례: 찰리 킴의 넥스트점프 평생 고용 정책은 직원을 가족처럼 대해요. 불균형적 보너스를 받는 은행 CEO들은 숫자를 위해 사람을 희생시키며 리더십의 사회적 계약을 위반했어요. 배리-웨밀러의 밥 채프먼은 2008년 불경기에 해고 대신 순환 휴직을 선택하며 '모두가 조금 고통받는 게 낫다'고 했어요 — 사기가 올랐고, 2천만 달러를 절약했으며, 직원들이 자발적으로 휴가를 교환했어요.
keyPoints: NextJump: lifetime employment, coaching instead of firing
Banking CEOs violated leadership by sacrificing people for personal gain
Bob Chapman chose furloughs over layoffs — 'all suffer a little'
Employees spontaneously traded furlough weeks to help each other

sections.section: Leadership Is a Choice, Not a Rank
sections.summary: Sinek declares that leadership is a choice, not a rank. True leaders are not those with authority, but those who choose to look after the people around them. He closes with a story of a Marine officer who ate last, and his men brought him food — because leaders go first, take risks first, and sacrifice first. When they do, people willingly give their blood, sweat, and tears in return.
sections.summaryKo: 사이넥은 리더십은 선택이지 직급이 아니라고 선언해요. 진정한 리더는 권한을 가진 사람이 아니라 주변 사람을 돌보기로 선택한 사람이에요. 마지막에 먹은 해병대 장교 이야기로 마무리해요 — 부하들이 음식을 가져다줬어요. 리더가 먼저 가고, 먼저 위험을 감수하고, 먼저 희생하면, 사람들은 기꺼이 피와 땀과 눈물로 보답해요.
keyPoints: Leadership is a choice, not a rank
Authority is not the same as leadership
True leaders look after the people around them
Marine officer ate last — his men brought him their food
Leaders go first, take risks first, sacrifice first
